content.text: The Okinawan しまくとぅば has a little over 13 short pages of vocabulary one must know, so this chapter will cover the first page (that start with あ and い). There might be some repeat, but the main point of this is to fully master the crucial Okinawan vocabulary for the test.
This first lesson is on the あ words:
あかさん - bright (both metaphorically and literally), or red (though in this case あかー is an alternative option).
あがり - east. The reverse is いり - west.
あじ - taste (same meaning as Japanese).
あっちゅん - to walk, but metaphorically it can mean to go and attend (a gathering/meeting/club, a school, etc.).
あらいん or あらゆん - to wash
あんら or あんだ - oil
